what_it_is.prose: Indrajaal is an autonomous counter-UAS platform developed by Grene Robotics (Hyderabad, est. 2008) and now commercialised by Indrajaal Drone Defence, a separate entity spun off from Grene Robotics in 2023. Founder & CEO Kiran Raju leads both companies. The manufacturing / integration partner is Sigma Advanced Systems. The platform comprises twelve modular technologies — greneOS, DefOS, HiveMind, Zombee, SkyCop, Brig, SpiderMesh, Repulsor, GreneEye, HyperSensing, WeaponFusion, and GlobalGrid — and is fielded in a 12-product family covering Infra (static infrastructure), Urban, Military, Ranger (mobile patrol vehicle), Trooper (manpack), Border, Combat (armoured), Zombee (autonomous interceptor drone), Maritime, and Repulsor (portable). Per the vendor, a single Indrajaal node can cover 4,000 sq.km. The HyperSensing suite combines acoustic sensors, active RF, passive RF, ESM, EO, and thermal sensors; the GreneEye module provides machine-vision classification. Soft-kill effectors include the Repulsor (tractor-beam jam and control) and Retractor (cyber takeover, guiding the hostile drone to a safe landing). Hard-kill is provided by the Zombee Level-5 autonomous interceptor drone, and WeaponFusion can make existing weapons autonomous. The Ranger (Anti-Drone Patrol Vehicle, ADPV) was launched in Hyderabad on 26 November 2025 with 10 km detection and 4 km mitigation range. Indrajaal's first deployment was for the Red Fort Independence Day celebrations in 2021, where it conducted a live intercept of multiple hostile drones. It is ARDTC-certified for deploying Counter-UAS systems. By April 2025, Indrajaal had deployments with the Indian Army, the Indonesian Army, the world's largest refinery (a private operator, covering an area bigger than London), and India's third-largest airport (37.5 million passengers). In late 2025, Indrajaal received ₹100 crore in orders from the Indian Army and Indian Navy, plus ₹155 crore in 2025-26 for the Ranger variant. The 'V1' label used in the Atlas is an editorial designation; Indrajaal does not version its platform publicly.

import_dependencies.summary: Per CEO Kiran Raju's April 2025 statement to the Times of India: 'The entire platform has been developed indigenously including the interceptors, but some components like sensors that are not made in India have been procured from friendly countries such as Israel.' The principal imported subsystem is therefore EO/IR sensors from Israel. No numerical indigenous content percentage has been disclosed. FPGA, GaN RF, and IMU dependencies are not publicly documented but follow industry-typical supply chains.

faq.question: Is Indrajaal made by Grene Robotics or Indrajaal Drone Defence?
faq.answer: Both — Indrajaal was originally developed by Grene Robotics (Hyderabad, est. 2008) under founder & CEO Kiran Raju. In 2023, Indrajaal Drone Defence was spun off as a separate entity (also led by Kiran Raju) to commercialise the platform. Manufacturing / integration partner is Sigma Advanced Systems. The two companies remain affiliated.

faq.question: What is the Zombee hard-kill interceptor?
faq.answer: Zombee is Indrajaal's Level-5 autonomous interceptor drone designed for surveillance and hard-kill engagements against hostile UAS. It is part of the 12-modular-technology Indrajaal platform and is one of two hard-kill options (the other being WeaponFusion, which makes existing weapons autonomous).

faq.question: Where is Indrajaal operationally deployed?
faq.answer: Indrajaal's first deployment was for the Red Fort Independence Day celebrations in 2021. By April 2025, confirmed deployments included the Indian Army, the Indonesian Army, the world's largest refinery (a private operator, covering an area bigger than London), and India's third-largest airport (37.5 million passengers per year). The Ranger mobile patrol variant was launched on 26 November 2025.
